newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU parliament attacks Beijing over Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament attacks Beijing over Hong Kong.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday condemned China's decision to replace Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council by a handpicked body ahead of the return of the territory to Chinese rule on July 1.

"The European Parliament regrets the Chinese government's decision to dissolve Hong Kong's elected Legislative Council and questions the legitimacy of the Provisional Legislative Council," the parliament said in a resolution.
The resolution demanded that Beijing fully respect the Sino- British Joint Declaration which sets out the terms of the handover to China of the British colony.
The directly elected European Union assembly also demanded free and fair elections within three months of Hong Kong's return to Chinese sovereignty.

"The future of Hong Kong and (former Portuguese colony) Macao and the maintenance of their political, social and economic freedom is a matter of determining importance for the European Union," the resolution said.

The resolution follows a debate on Wednesday on the future of EU relations with Hong Kong, in which deputies voiced fears about Beijing's plans and urged the EU's executive European Commission to monitor annually "political, economic and human rights developments" in the territory.

They also criticised the Dutch presidency of the EU for assuming China would really respect the principle of "one country, two systems" and allow Hong Kong to retain its current political and economic set up.
On Wednesday Beijing announced planned curbs on Hong Kong civil liberties, justifying them on the grounds that foreign forces posed risks to "national security".
The proposals were slammed as open to abuse and retrograde by the democracy movement, pressure groups, departing colonial Governor Chris Patten and the Hong Kong press.
The changes would bar overseas funding of local political groups and grant police sweeping powers to ban demonstrations.
Dutch European Affairs Minister Michael Patijn told the parliament on Wednesday there was much less concern inside Hong Kong than abroad about the future Beijing was planning for the territory.
But British Liberal Graham Watson, who visited the colony last month, insisted there was real fear among Hong Kong's six million citizens about life under Chinese rule.
